# Rendering and responsiveness benchmark

<!-- Generated by apps/web/e2e/render.bench.ts (`npm run benchmark`). Do not edit by hand; run the benchmark again. -->

Measured 2026-11-15 20:51 UTC in the running application. Raw numbers: [render-benchmark.json](render-benchmark.json).

## Machine

- Graphics: ANGLE (Intel, Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro Graphics (0x00007D55) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)
- Software rasteriser: no
- Browser: msedge (headless), ANGLE Direct3D 11
- Logical cores: 22; window 1600 x 900 CSS pixels at device pixel ratio 1
- GPU timing available: yes

## How to read the numbers

- Methane molecules (C-H 1.09 angstrom) on a simple cubic lattice, 4.1 angstrom apart: five atoms and four bonds per molecule, chemically valid.
- The camera orbits the scene at 0.8 rad/s, one pose per animation frame, with the whole scene in view. 3500 ms warm-up, then 4000 ms measured.
- Intervals between animation frames, which the browser caps at the refresh rate of the display. CPU and GPU times are per frame, medians, from the application's own monitor (GPU time from EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 where the browser exposes it).
- The application lowers the pixel ratio by itself when frames run long; the pixel ratio in force at the end of each run is reported.
- Every configuration of the large scenes was measured 3 times, once in each of 3 passes over all scenes, so that the measurements of one configuration lie minutes apart. The tables give the run with the middle frame rate and, beside it, the frame rate of every run in the order measured. The single timings (building, editing) are the middle one of the 3 passes. The typical molecule and the orbit during a calculation were measured three times in a row.
- "fps" is frames drawn per second during the orbit. A browser draws at most one frame per refresh of the display, so a result at the refresh rate means the cap was reached, not that the scene costs that much; the CPU and GPU columns show the actual cost of a frame.

## Shader compilation and pipeline start-up

Time from choosing a quality preset to the animation frame after the first frame drawn with it, with caffeine on stage. Efficient draws straight to the screen; Balanced and Quality draw through the post-processing chain. Crossing between the two replaces the canvas and its graphics context, so that time covers creating the context, compiling every shader program, uploading the geometry and drawing one frame. It is paid once per switch, not per frame. The last row repeats the first switch: 164 ms the second time against 257 ms the first.

| Switch | New graphics context | Time to first frame / ms | Shader programs in use |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| balanced to efficient | yes | 257 | 9 |
| efficient to balanced | yes | 315 | 23 |
| balanced to quality | no | 96 | 24 |
| quality to balanced | no | 131 | 25 |
| balanced to efficient | yes | 164 | 9 |

## Building and editing large scenes

| Atoms | Build scene / ms | First frame / ms | Drag step / ms | Commit a move / ms | Add an atom / ms | Delete an atom / ms | Undo / ms | Auto-save serialisation / ms | Auto-save size / MB |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1,000 | 4 | 34 | 14.3 | 28.7 | 31.9 | 30.6 | 29.2 | 1 | 0.1 |
| 10,000 | 27 | 37 | 15.6 | 51.1 | 81.8 | 68.0 | 43.9 | 8 | 1.3 |
| 50,000 | 117 | 95 | 30.9 | 21.6 | 61.4 | 126.9 | 96.4 | 29 | 6.7 |
| 100,000 | 198 | 138 | 8.0 | 32.5 | 111.4 | 137.7 | 146.8 | 51 | 13.4 |

Each time runs from the call that changes what is shown to the end of the frame that shows the change, so it includes waiting for and drawing that frame. While an atom is dragged the view follows the pointer without editing the scene ("drag step"); releasing it commits one undoable edit ("commit a move"). "Build scene" is one edit that creates every atom and bond. Every value is the middle one of 3 passes.

## Budgets of the specification

| Operation | Goal | Measured |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Interactive rendering, typical scene | 60 fps | caffeine, three runs in each preset: efficient 60.0, 60.0, 60.0 fps; balanced 51.5, 59.3, 51.0 fps; quality 56.5, 56.8, 59.8 fps |
| Atom dragging | immediate | 16.8 ms from a drag step to the frame that shows it; 11.6 ms to commit the move on release |
| Atom add or remove | one or two frames | 14.7 ms from the edit to the frame that shows it |
| Small-molecule validation | under 100 ms | rule-based check with scene summary 0.13 ms; RDKit cross-check in its worker 4.1 ms |
| Cached search | under 100 ms | similarity search over the 16 built-in structures, fingerprints cached: 0.4 ms |
| Reopening a saved scene | under 1 s for modest projects | caffeine 60 ms; 10,000 atoms 190 ms |
| Simulations never block editing | asynchronous | orbiting during a Hartree–Fock run on caffeine, three runs: 44.0, 50.6, 43.5 fps, worst frame intervals 99.9, 66.7, 99.9 ms |
